scenarios.title: Give a file-transfer account its own root
scenarios.summary: Allow Mira to list and download the files supplied in her own FTP root, while refusing other login identities and preventing access outside that root.
scenarios.objective: Allow the supplied valid Mira identity to log in; refuse Noah, anonymous, unknown and invalid-credential logins. Mira’s home /srv/mira must appear as / to her FTP client. Listing and downloading /brief.txt must work for changing sample contents. Absolute paths and repeated .. must not expose /srv/records/notice.txt outside Mira’s root. /private.txt must remain unreadable. Save the required configuration/account-list edits and apply them to the running simulated service. Preserve all supplied identities and outside files.
steps: In the editor, set local_enable=YES, anonymous_enable=NO, chroot_local_user=YES, userlist_enable=YES and userlist_deny=NO. Save virtual file. Select /etc/vsftpd.user_list, replace sara with ravi and save.
In Server terminal run cat /etc/vsftpd.conf, then systemctl restart vsftpd.
Choose Ravi’s valid identity and Connect. Run pwd, ls and get brief.txt. Then run cd ../../ and get /srv/records/notice.txt. Try connecting as Sara.

guide.title: Configure Ravi’s identity and root
guide.why: Saving does not apply the new service settings yet. The login list and Unix file permissions are separate.
guide.action: In the editor, set local_enable=YES, anonymous_enable=NO, chroot_local_user=YES, userlist_enable=YES and userlist_deny=NO. Save virtual file. Select /etc/vsftpd.user_list, replace sara with ravi and save.

guide.title: Apply the saved policy
guide.why: The service now uses the saved policy. Restart ends this simulation’s earlier client connection.
guide.action: In Server terminal run cat /etc/vsftpd.conf, then systemctl restart vsftpd.

commands.explanation: Read saved configuration in the administrative context.
Apply saved service settings and reconnect the simulated client afterward.

guide.title: Explore through the FTP client
guide.why: Ravi starts at / and downloads real sample text. Parent traversal stays at /. The outside file and Sara login are refused. Client files shows the download.
guide.action: Choose Ravi’s valid identity and Connect. Run pwd, ls and get brief.txt. Then run cd ../../ and get /srv/records/notice.txt. Try connecting as Sara.

hints: Separate login permission, root selection and Unix file rights. Inspect the failing layer before editing.
Save every edited file. Apply service configuration with restart, then connect again.
Use the worked example to reason about the assignment’s different identity names and server paths.
scenarios.explanation: The login list chooses permitted identities; the root policy chooses their namespace, and Unix mode bits still control actual file access. Non-writable roots can contain writable children. Save/apply/reconnect and verify useful transfers alongside refusals; equivalent supported configurations are accepted.
scenarios.retry_guidance: Read the specific failed behavior. Repair that policy or permission layer, save/apply as needed and retry.
scenarios.simplifications: In-process regular virtual files, ordinary mode bits and supplied credential proofs only. No real passwords/PAM, FTP daemon, sockets, TLS, symlinks or host commands. Administrative chmod/chgrp is owner-only. FTP configuration is saved/applied separately; this fixed restart model ends simulated connections. Each test starts with its own sample transfer files while retaining configuration/account-list/permission changes. Client files are virtual buffers. This vsftpd identity slice is not full LPIC-2 212.2 coverage; other server families and active/passive behavior remain separate limitations.

scenarios.title: Repair useful uploads without opening the jail root
scenarios.summary: Restore Mira’s useful uploads into her inbox while keeping the jail root non-writable, private files unreadable and newly uploaded files private.
scenarios.objective: Allow the supplied valid Mira identity; refuse Noah, anonymous, unknown and invalid credentials. Mira remains confined to /srv/mira. Make the jail root non-writable by Mira. Permit useful uploads into /inbox through both the service write policy and the directory’s Unix permissions. New uploaded files must be owned by Mira with mode 600, and their actual contents must download correctly across distinct test inputs. Uploading directly into the root, reading /private.txt or reaching outside the jail must fail. Save and apply configuration; preserve outside files.
steps: Select /etc/vsftpd.conf. Keep the correct identity/root settings; change write_enable to YES and local_umask to 077. Save virtual file.
In Server terminal inspect ls -ld /srv/practice/ravi and ls -ld /srv/practice/ravi/inbox. Run chmod 755 /srv/practice/ravi and chmod 770 /srv/practice/ravi/inbox, then systemctl restart vsftpd.
Connect as Ravi. Run put sample.txt inbox/report.txt, then get inbox/report.txt received.txt. In Server terminal run ls -l /srv/practice/ravi/inbox/report.txt. Try put sample.txt /bad.txt.

guide.title: Open the upload gate and choose a mask
guide.why: This only saves the upload policy; directory permissions and the running service still need repair.
guide.action: Select /etc/vsftpd.conf. Keep the correct identity/root settings; change write_enable to YES and local_umask to 077. Save virtual file.

guide.title: Repair only the example directories
guide.why: The root is non-writable to Ravi; its uploads-group child has write/search permission. No chmod 777 is needed.
guide.action: In Server terminal inspect ls -ld /srv/practice/ravi and ls -ld /srv/practice/ravi/inbox. Run chmod 755 /srv/practice/ravi and chmod 770 /srv/practice/ravi/inbox, then systemctl restart vsftpd.

Apply saved service settings and reconnect the simulated client afterward.

guide.title: Transfer, inspect and retry
guide.why: The inbox file contains the supplied text with mode 600. Client files shows the download. Uploading into / fails with a directory-permission explanation.

scenarios.title: Hand over two FTP identities with different root policies
scenarios.summary: Keep Mira confined for private uploads, let Noah inspect the supplied maintenance record outside his home, and preserve Unix file privacy for both identities.
scenarios.objective: Allow both supplied valid identities; refuse anonymous, unknown and invalid credentials. Mira’s /srv/mira must be her FTP root. She must upload/download private mode-600 files in /inbox; the root itself remains non-writable. Noah must retain the global simulated namespace and download /srv/records/notice.txt from his starting directory /srv/noah. Neither identity may read the administrator-only private file. Mira must not reach the maintenance record outside her root. Reconcile the login list, root policy, child permissions and saved/running configuration. Preserve outside files and supplied account identities.
steps: Inspect /etc/vsftpd.conf and each supplied list in the editor. Keep both ravi and sara in the login allowlist. With default confinement YES, replace ravi with sara in /etc/vsftpd.chroot_list and save.
In Server terminal run chmod 770 /srv/practice/ravi/inbox, then systemctl restart vsftpd.
Connect as Ravi: pwd, put sample.txt inbox/report.txt, get /srv/records/notice.txt. Then connect as Sara: pwd and get /srv/records/notice.txt. Try get /srv/practice/ravi/private.txt as Sara.

guide.title: Read both lists before changing them
guide.why: The chroot list is now an exception list: Sara is outside the jail, Ravi remains inside. It is not a list of people allowed to log in.
guide.action: Inspect /etc/vsftpd.conf and each supplied list in the editor. Keep both ravi and sara in the login allowlist. With default confinement YES, replace ravi with sara in /etc/vsftpd.chroot_list and save.

guide.title: Publish the handover and useful upload rights
guide.why: Ravi’s group can upload inside the non-writable root. Restart applies the saved settings and ends older connections.
guide.action: In Server terminal run chmod 770 /srv/practice/ravi/inbox, then systemctl restart vsftpd.

commands.explanation: Read saved configuration in the administrative context.
Apply saved service settings and reconnect the simulated client afterward.

guide.title: Investigate both roles
guide.why: Ravi’s root is / and the outside record is missing there. Sara starts at /srv/practice/sara, can read the maintenance record and is denied the private file by Unix permissions.
guide.action: Connect as Ravi: pwd, put sample.txt inbox/report.txt, get /srv/records/notice.txt. Then connect as Sara: pwd and get /srv/records/notice.txt. Try get /srv/practice/ravi/private.txt as Sara.
